title: Buffers for Use in Biological Systems
author: Neilier Junior
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfsdjna6

steps.title: Prepare KCl/HCl buffer (pH 1–2.2)
steps.instruction: Make a 0.1 M potassium chloride solution by dissolving 7.45 g KCl (M.W. 74.5 g mol⁻¹) per litre of deionized water. Prepare 0.1 M hydrochloric acid. Mix 50 mL of the KCl solution with the indicated volume of HCl, bring the mixture to 100 mL with deionized water, and adjust the pH to the desired value between 1.0 and 2.2 using a calibrated pH meter.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 0.1 M KCl stock (7.45 g L⁻¹, M.W. 74.5 g mol⁻¹).
Prepare 0.1 M HCl stock.
Mix 50 mL KCl solution with appropriate HCl volume, bring to 100 mL, and adjust pH.

steps.title: Prepare Glycine/HCl buffer (pH 2.2–3.6)
steps.instruction: Make a 0.1 M glycine solution by dissolving 7.5 g glycine (M.W. 75.0 g mol⁻¹) per litre. Prepare 0.1 M hydrochloric acid. Mix 50 mL of the glycine solution with the indicated volume of HCl, adjust the final volume to 100 mL with deionized water, and set the pH to the desired value between 2.2 and 3.6 with a sensitive pH meter.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 0.1 M glycine stock (7.5 g L⁻¹, M.W. 75.0 g mol⁻¹).
Prepare 0.1 M HCl stock.
Mix 50 mL glycine solution with appropriate HCl volume, bring to 100 mL, and adjust pH.

steps.title: Prepare Citric‑Citrate buffer (pH 3.0–6.2)
steps.instruction: Prepare 0.1 M citric acid by dissolving 19.21 g citric acid (M.W. 192.1 g mol⁻¹) per litre and 0.1 M sodium citrate dihydrate by dissolving 29.4 g (M.W. 294.0 g mol⁻¹) per litre. Mix the two solutions in the proportions required for the target pH, adjust the final volume to 100 mL with deionized water, and fine‑tune the pH (3.0–6.2) with a calibrated pH meter. **Do not use the pentahydrate form of sodium citrate.**

substeps.instruction: Prepare 0.1 M citric acid stock (19.21 g L⁻¹, M.W. 192.1 g mol⁻¹).
Prepare 0.1 M sodium citrate dihydrate stock (29.4 g L⁻¹, M.W. 294.0 g mol⁻¹).
Mix stocks in required ratio, bring to 100 mL, and adjust pH.

steps.title: Prepare Acetate buffer (pH 3.6–5.6)
steps.instruction: Make a 0.1 M acetic acid solution by diluting 5.8 mL of glacial acetic acid to 1 L with deionized water. Prepare 0.1 M sodium acetate either as anhydrous (8.2 g L⁻¹, M.W. 82.0 g mol⁻¹) or trihydrate (13.6 g L⁻¹, M.W. 136.0 g mol⁻¹). Mix the acetic acid and sodium acetate solutions in the proportions required for the desired pH, adjust the final volume to 100 mL with deionized water, and set the pH (3.6–5.6) using a sensitive pH meter.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 0.1 M acetic acid stock (5.8 mL to 1 L).
Prepare 0.1 M sodium acetate stock (either 8.2 g L⁻¹ anhydrous or 13.6 g L⁻¹ trihydrate).
Mix stocks in required ratio, bring to 100 mL, and adjust pH.

steps.title: Prepare Citric‑Phosphate buffer (pH 2.6–7.0)
steps.instruction: Prepare 0.1 M citric acid (19.21 g L⁻¹, M.W. 192.1 g mol⁻¹) and 0.2 M dibasic sodium phosphate either as dihydrate (35.6 g L⁻¹, M.W. 178.0 g mol⁻¹) or heptahydrate (53.6 g L⁻¹, M.W. 268.0 g mol⁻¹). Mix the two solutions in the proportions indicated for the target pH, adjust the final volume to 100 mL with deionized water, and fine‑tune the pH (2.6–7.0) with a calibrated pH meter.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 0.1 M citric acid stock (19.21 g L⁻¹, M.W. 192.1 g mol⁻¹).
Prepare 0.2 M sodium phosphate stock (35.6 g L⁻¹ dihydrate or 53.6 g L⁻¹ heptahydrate).
Mix stocks in required ratio, bring to 100 mL, and adjust pH.

steps.title: Prepare Sodium phosphate buffer (pH 5.8–8.0)
steps.instruction: Make 0.1 M sodium phosphate monobasic by dissolving 13.8 g L⁻¹ (monohydrate, M.W. 138.0 g mol⁻¹) and 0.1 M sodium phosphate dibasic by dissolving 26.8 g L⁻¹ (heptahydrate, M.W. 268.0 g mol⁻¹). Mix the two solutions in the proportions required for the desired pH, adjust the final volume to 200 mL with deionized water, and set the pH (5.8–8.0) using a sensitive pH meter.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 0.1 M monobasic stock (13.8 g L⁻¹, M.W. 138.0 g mol⁻¹).
Prepare 0.1 M dibasic stock (26.8 g L⁻¹, M.W. 268.0 g mol⁻¹).
Mix stocks in required ratio, bring to 200 mL, and adjust pH.

steps.title: Prepare Tris‑HCl buffer (pH 7.2–9.0)
steps.instruction: Prepare 0.1 M Tris(hydroxymethyl)aminomethane by dissolving 12.1 g L⁻¹ (M.W. 121.0 g mol⁻¹). Prepare 0.1 M hydrochloric acid. Mix 50 mL of the Tris solution with the indicated volume of HCl, bring the mixture to 200 mL with deionized water, and adjust the pH to the desired value between 7.2 and 9.0 using a calibrated pH meter.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 0.1 M Tris stock (12.1 g L⁻¹, M.W. 121.0 g mol⁻¹).
Prepare 0.1 M HCl stock.
Mix 50 mL Tris with appropriate HCl volume, bring to 200 mL, and adjust pH.

steps.title: Prepare Glycine/NaOH buffer (pH 8.6–10.6)
steps.instruction: Make a 0.1 M glycine solution by dissolving 7.5 g L⁻¹ (M.W. 75.0 g mol⁻¹) and a 0.1 M sodium hydroxide solution by dissolving 4.0 g L⁻¹ (M.W. 40.0 g mol⁻¹). Mix 50 mL of the glycine solution with the indicated volume of NaOH solution, adjust the final volume to 200 mL with deionized water, and set the pH to the desired value between 8.6 and 10.6 using a calibrated pH meter.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 0.1 M glycine stock (7.5 g L⁻¹, M.W. 75.0 g mol⁻¹).
Prepare 0.1 M NaOH stock (4.0 g L⁻¹, M.W. 40.0 g mol⁻¹).
Mix 50 mL glycine with appropriate NaOH volume, bring to 200 mL, and adjust pH.

steps.title: Prepare Carbonate buffer (pH 9.2–10.6)
steps.instruction: Prepare 0.1 M sodium carbonate (anhydrous) by dissolving 10.6 g L⁻¹ (M.W. 106.0 g mol⁻¹) and 0.1 M sodium bicarbonate by dissolving 8.4 g L⁻¹ (M.W. 84.0 g mol⁻¹). Mix the two solutions in the proportions indicated for the target pH, adjust the final volume to 200 mL with deionized water, and fine‑tune the pH (9.2–10.6) using a calibrated pH meter.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 0.1 M sodium carbonate stock (10.6 g L⁻¹, M.W. 106.0 g mol⁻¹).
Prepare 0.1 M sodium bicarbonate stock (8.4 g L⁻¹, M.W. 84.0 g mol⁻¹).
Mix stocks in required ratio, bring to 200 mL, and adjust pH.

steps.title: Prepare 1 L standard PBS (pH 7.4)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 8.7 g NaCl, 1.82 g potassium phosphate tribasic trihydrate (K₂HPO₄·3H₂O), and 0.23 g potassium dihydrogen phosphate (KH₂PO₄) in deionized water and make up the solution to a final volume of 1 L. Adjust the pH to 7.4 with a calibrated pH meter before use.

substeps.instruction: Weigh and add 8.7 g NaCl, 1.82 g K₂HPO₄·3H₂O, and 0.23 g KH₂PO₄ to a container.
Add deionized water and bring volume to 1 L.
Adjust pH to 7.4 with a pH meter.

steps.title: Prepare alternative PBS formulation (pH 7.4)
steps.instruction: Prepare a phosphate‑buffered saline solution containing 137 mM NaCl, 2.7 mM KCl, 10 mM Na₂HPO₄, and 1.76 mM KH₂PO₄ in 1 L of distilled water. Adjust the pH to 7.4 before use.

substeps.instruction: Calculate and dissolve the salts to give the listed molarities in 1 L water.
Adjust pH to 7.4 with a calibrated pH meter.

steps.title: Prepare 1 L TBS (pH 7.4)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1.21 g Tris base and 8.7 g NaCl in deionized water and bring the volume to 1 L. Adjust the pH to 7.4 with a calibrated pH meter. Note: Tris has a pKₐ of 8.3, so its buffering capacity at pH 7.4 is minimal compared with phosphate buffers (pKₐ = 7.21).

substeps.instruction: Weigh and add 1.21 g Tris base and 8.7 g NaCl to a container.
Add deionized water and bring volume to 1 L.
Adjust pH to 7.4 with a pH meter.
